criteria.4: persistent benign update can survive across episode/task boundary
criteria.5: update target can be named before post-update outcome
criteria.6: pre/post collateral change can be measured
criteria.8: target gain separable from non-target regression
criteria.11: collateral damage detectable beyond terminal success
criteria.25: license sufficiently clear for static/preflight use
criteria.28: not intrinsically dependent on expensive proprietary APIs
criteria.29: state reset reliable enough for causal design
criteria.33: mechanism can generalize beyond benchmark-specific trick
criteria.34: primary effect can be identified without benchmark leaderboard semantics

rating_legend.STRONG: native or directly supported by released benchmark/environment
rating_legend.PARTIAL: possible with a bounded extension or has an identified qualification risk
rating_legend.WEAK: not naturally supported or creates a major causal-identification problem

matrix.name: AppWorld + AppWorld-UL semantics
matrix.publication: AppWorld: ACL 2024 Long Paper; AppWorld-UL: ICML 2026
matrix.why: Released multi-app databases, task generators, database checkpoint/revert, and state-based unit tests already support expected-state and unexpected-state checks. AppWorld-UL adds natural ambiguity, confirmation, infeasibility, and constraint semantics.
matrix.critical_risk: Persistent self-update is not native. The public repository also notes protected bundle components under a different license, so exact data/bundle terms must be re-audited before execution.
matrix.required_modification: Create AppWorld-Externality as an explicitly benchmark-derived controlled train/dev substrate. The only cross-episode persistent state is one content-addressed agent-side procedural repair artifact; all constraint and edge definitions are compiled before model outcomes. Do not claim official AppWorld leaderboard identity.

matrix.name: ToolSandbox
matrix.why: Native world-state snapshots plus Milestone DAG evaluation make prerequisite topology and intermediate-state evaluation unusually explicit.
matrix.critical_risk: Narrower application world, built-in user-simulator variation, and a custom Apple source license reduce the attractiveness of making it the sole primary substrate.
matrix.required_modification: Add one agent-side persistent procedural repair layer and construct matched scenario variants from the released scenario schema; keep user-simulator variation outside the primary causal contrast where possible.

matrix.name: WorkArena++ on BrowserGym
matrix.why: WorkArena++ is explicitly compositional, with validated subtasks and fixed configurations in realistic enterprise workflows, making chain and hub dependencies natural.
matrix.critical_risk: Browser perception, ServiceNow deployment state, UI variation, and reset fidelity can be confounded with update externality.
matrix.required_modification: Use only after the primary mechanism contract is frozen; externalize one persistent procedural repair state and map subtask validators to constraint predicates.

matrix.name: tau3-bench current implementation / original tau-bench lineage
matrix.publication: Original tau-bench: ICLR 2025; current tau3-bench: living 2026 successor implementation with separately released components
matrix.why: Customer-service policies, state-changing APIs, and database outcomes are attractive, but current repository lineage has moved beyond the original ICLR 2025 benchmark and per-constraint topology is not a native evaluation object.
matrix.critical_risk: User-simulator/protocol variability plus versioned grading changes complicate a first causal identification.
matrix.required_modification: Pin current tau3 code/data separately from the ICLR 2025 publication identity and add preregistered per-constraint environment assertions before any scientific use.

matrix.name: SkillLearnBench
matrix.why: It is a close continual-skill benchmark with deterministic verifiers and persistent skill generation, but heterogeneous tasks do not provide a naturally randomized shared-state constraint graph.
matrix.critical_risk: Forcing independent/chain/hub topology onto unrelated tasks would turn the mechanism into a benchmark-specific construction artifact.
matrix.required_modification: Reserve for post-mechanism validation of the already-frozen procedural update surface.

matrix.name: WebArena-Verified
matrix.publication: Verified browser benchmark release; not used as the primary formal-publication anchor here
matrix.why: Deterministic browser evaluation is useful for robustness checks, but persistent self-update and controllable constraint topology are not native constructs.
matrix.critical_risk: Topology would have to be retrofitted rather than generated from the benchmark semantics.
matrix.required_modification: Use only as later browser robustness validation.

matrix.name: OSWorld / OSWorld-Verified
matrix.publication: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track; OSWorld-Verified is a later benchmark revision
matrix.why: Excellent real-world external validity but GUI grounding, VM state, application drift, and visual perception can mimic or hide update externality.
matrix.critical_risk: Causal mechanism failure cannot be cleanly separated from GUI/environment failure in a first experiment.
matrix.required_modification: Reserve for late external validation only if the mechanism survives in a controlled substrate.

matrix.name: BrowserGym framework
matrix.publication: Execution/evaluation framework in the ServiceNow browser-agent ecosystem
matrix.why: Useful harness, but not one canonical environment with a constraint ontology.
matrix.critical_risk: Framework-level behavior could be mistakenly presented as a benchmark result.
matrix.required_modification: Use only as a harness around a separately selected browser substrate.

ranking.name: AppWorld + AppWorld-UL semantics
ranking.critical_advantage: Native database-state evaluator, checkpoint/revert, collateral-damage tests, and a public task-generator extension path.
ranking.critical_risk: Persistent update is an extension; exact bundle/data license and derived task-family semantics must be re-audited before execution.

ranking.name: ToolSandbox
ranking.critical_advantage: Native Milestone DAG and per-turn state snapshots make dependency topology exceptionally explicit.
ranking.critical_risk: Narrower world, user-simulator variation, and custom Apple source license.
ranking.required_modification: Agent-side persistent procedural repair plus matched scenario topology variants.

ranking.name: WorkArena++ on BrowserGym
ranking.critical_advantage: Validated compositional enterprise subtasks naturally realize prerequisite/workflow structure.
ranking.critical_risk: Browser/UI/ServiceNow reset and grounding noise can mask update externality.
ranking.required_modification: Freeze primary mechanism first; use subtask validators and a persistent procedural layer.

selected.name: AppWorld-Externality
selected.parent: AppWorld ACL 2024; AppWorld-UL ICML 2026 is a constraint-semantics reference
selected.persistent_update_extension: One agent-side content-addressed procedural repair artifact persists while each environment replay returns to its frozen initial state.
why_selected: State-based unit tests can expose newly violated non-target obligations rather than only terminal success.
Database checkpoint/revert supports exact before/after replay from a frozen initial task state.
Task generators expose setup, validation solution, evaluation, and metadata, enabling outcome-blind matched task-family construction on released train/dev material.
Nine simulated apps and 100+ database tables provide natural shared-state and shared-API dependencies without live-web drift.
ACL 2024 AppWorld plus ICML 2026 AppWorld-UL provide broad current agent audience and natural constraint/confirmation semantics.
